title: Archive

page.title: Archive
page.description: Search and read the tenant's archived mail and verify the hash chain. Retention and legal holds are set in the tenant's archive settings.

noTenant: Select a tenant to search its archive.
forbidden: Archive search requires the tenant administrator role.

search.placeholder: Search subject, sender, recipients and body
search.empty: No archived mail matches this search.
search.emptyTenant: Nothing has been archived for this tenant yet.
search.invertedRange: The end date is before the start date, so nothing can match.
search.loadErrorDescription: The result is unknown. It does not mean that nothing is archived.
search.includeSupersededHint: A mail captured again by a stronger way is listed once; this also lists the earlier, weaker capture.

detail.title: Message
detail.empty: Select a message in the list to read it.
detail.loadError: The details of this message could not be loaded
detail.previewError: The content could not be read
detail.attachmentsNote: Attachments are included in the .eml file.
detail.downloadHint: The original message as archived, with all attachments. It is compared with its checksum before the download, and the download is recorded in the audit log.
detail.sourceSmtpForward: Copy forwarded by the mail provider
detail.supersedesLink: the earlier capture of this mail
detail.supersededByLink: a stronger capture of this mail

chain.title: Hash chain
chain.description: Checks that the archive's entries are chained without a gap, compares the chain with the daily anchors sealed every night and, on request, reads a sample of the messages back from storage.
chain.verifyWithContent: Verify chain and a sample of the content
chain.contentHint: The sample reads up to {count} randomly chosen messages from storage and compares each with its size and SHA-256 at capture.
chain.loadError: The check could not be run
chain.empty: Nothing to verify yet: the archive is empty.

links.ok: Links: {count, plural, one {# entry} other {all # entries}} chained without a gap. This checked the checksums stored in the database.
links.broken: Chain broken at entry {position} of {total}: “{subject}”, received on {date}.

anchors.none: Daily anchors: none sealed yet. Until the first anchor is sealed overnight, entries removed from the end of the chain cannot be detected.
anchors.ok: Daily anchors: {checked, plural, one {# anchor} other {# anchors}} compared, the newest from {date}.
anchors.unsealed: {count, plural, one {# entry is} other {# entries are}} newer than the last anchor and not covered by it yet.
anchors.missing: Daily anchor of {date}: the chain is shorter than sealed then ({entries} entries). Entries are missing.
anchors.mismatch: Daily anchor of {date}: the chain differs at entry {entries} from the state sealed then.

content.skipped: Content: not read. The check above covers only the checksums in the database. Whether the messages in storage are unchanged is what the sample shows.
content.ok: Content: {count, plural, one {# message} other {# messages}} read from storage, each matches its checksum.
content.failed: Content: {failed} of {total} messages read do not match their checksum or could not be read.
content.notRecorded: {count, plural, one {# message of the sample was archived before its repository was recorded and could not be compared.} other {# messages of the sample were archived before their repository was recorded and could not be compared.}}
content.none: Content: no message of the sample could be compared.

legalHold.title: Legal holds
legalHold.description: While a legal hold is active, {appName} deletes none of the messages it covers, even when their retention has already ended. How well the storage itself protects against changes is shown in the archive under Protection of the archive storage.
legalHold.mailboxRemoved: A mailbox that is no longer protected
legalHold.empty: No legal holds for this tenant.
legalHold.loadError: The legal holds could not be loaded
legalHold.createFailed: The legal hold could not be placed

releaseDialog.title: Release legal hold?
releaseDialog.description: After the release, the deletion run can remove messages whose retention has ended and that no other legal hold covers. This cannot be undone.
releaseDialog.reasonHint: The reason is recorded in the audit log.

journal.title: Exchange journaling
journal.description: Exchange Online sends a copy of every message to this address before users see it. The archive keeps each copy until its retention ends, and the hash chain makes later changes detectable.

status.stale: No report for more than 24 hours

journal.notConfigured: Journaling is not set up on this installation. It needs JOURNAL_SMTP_PORT, JOURNAL_HOSTNAME and a TLS certificate for that host name, then a restart of the api. The guide below covers the Exchange Online side.

reason.restart_required: The license includes the journal receiver, but the api started before it was installed. Restart the api to start the receiver.
reason.listen_failed: The receiver could not start. Check the api log: usual causes are a port that is already in use or no permission for port 25.
reason.tls_not_configured: The receiver is not running because it has no TLS certificate. Exchange Online requires TLS for journal delivery, and {appName} never accepts journal mail without a certificate of your own. Set JOURNAL_TLS_CERT_PATH and JOURNAL_TLS_KEY_PATH to the PEM certificate chain and private key for the journal host name, then restart the api.
reason.tls_invalid: The receiver is not running because its TLS certificate cannot be used. JOURNAL_TLS_CERT_PATH and JOURNAL_TLS_KEY_PATH must both be set and point to readable PEM files, the private key must not be encrypted and must belong to the certificate. The api log names the file. Fix it, then restart the api.
reason.tls_expired: The TLS certificate of the receiver has expired, so Exchange Online cannot deliver. Replace the certificate and key files (JOURNAL_TLS_CERT_PATH and JOURNAL_TLS_KEY_PATH). A running receiver picks up renewed files within a few minutes; if it did not start, restart the api.
reason.not_started: The receiver has not started in this api process. If this stays after a reload, restart the api and read its log.

address.label: Journal address
address.hostMissing: No journal host name is configured, so there is no complete address yet. Set JOURNAL_HOSTNAME to the host name Exchange Online should deliver to, for example archive.example.com, and restart the api.
address.hostInvalid: JOURNAL_HOSTNAME is not a valid host name. Give the host name only: no scheme, path, port or mail address.

rotate.title: Rotate the journal address?
rotate.description: A new address is created and the current one stops working at once.
rotate.consequence: Until you change the recipient of your journal rule to the new address, reports are refused and not archived. Exchange Online sends them to the mailbox for undeliverable journal reports.
rotate.done: New journal address created. Update your journal rule.

checklist.title: What Exchange Online needs from this installation
checklist.dns: Publish {host} in DNS (an A or AAAA record, or an MX record that points to a host with one) and point it to this server.
checklist.dnsUnset: Publish the journal host name in DNS (an A or AAAA record, or an MX record that points to a host with one) once JOURNAL_HOSTNAME is set.
checklist.portOk: The receiver listens on port 25, the only port Exchange Online delivers to. It must be reachable from the internet.
checklist.portForward: Exchange Online delivers to port 25 only, but the receiver listens on port {port}. Forward port 25 of the public address to port {port} or set JOURNAL_SMTP_PORT=25.
checklist.portUnset: Exchange Online delivers to port 25 only. Set JOURNAL_SMTP_PORT=25 to start the receiver there.
checklist.tlsOk: TLS is required: the receiver refuses mail until the sender has started STARTTLS. The certificate must come from a publicly trusted authority and match the journal host name.
checklist.tlsNeeded: Exchange Online requires TLS. Provide a certificate and key for the journal host name and set JOURNAL_TLS_CERT_PATH and JOURNAL_TLS_KEY_PATH.
checklist.tlsMissing: No usable TLS certificate is configured (JOURNAL_TLS_CERT_PATH and JOURNAL_TLS_KEY_PATH), so the receiver does not offer TLS. The connector below requires TLS, so Exchange Online would not deliver.
checklist.size: Reports up to {size} MB are accepted; larger ones are refused.

guide.title: Set up Exchange Online
guide.intro: You need a connector that delivers to {appName} over TLS and a journal rule that sends every message through it. A Microsoft 365 administrator sets up both.

connector.title: Create a connector
connector.body: In the Exchange admin center (admin.exchange.microsoft.com) open Mail flow, then Connectors, and add a connector from Office 365 to Partner organization. Name it, for example, {appName} journal.

routing.title: Route it to the journal host
routing.body: Use the connector only for email sent to the domain {host} and route it through the smart host {host}. Always use TLS, with a certificate issued by a trusted authority whose name matches {host}. That domain must not be one of your accepted domains in Microsoft 365.

validate.title: Validate the connector
validate.body: Microsoft asks for an email address to test the connector: enter the journal address above. The test message arrives as a journal report that cannot be read and is archived with a flag. That is expected.

undeliverable.title: Name a mailbox for undeliverable reports
undeliverable.body: In the Microsoft Purview portal (purview.microsoft.com) open Data lifecycle management, then Exchange (legacy), then Journal rules. Under Send undeliverable journal reports to, enter a real mailbox that somebody reads, for example a shared mailbox. Exchange Online sends reports there that it could not deliver to {appName}, so this is where a gap shows up.

rule.title: Create the journal rule
rule.body: Add a rule that sends journal reports to the journal address above, for messages sent or received by everyone, of the type All messages. Turn the rule on.

verify.title: Check that it works
verify.body: Send a message inside your organization. The report usually arrives within a few minutes. This page then shows Receiving, and the message is in the archive search with the source Exchange Online journal.

hostNote.title: Journal host
hostNote.description: The name Exchange Online delivers its journal reports to. It is the same for every tenant of this server.

job.title: Journaling in Exchange
job.description: Exchange delivers this tenant's journal reports to this address. Set up the connector and the journal rule once per tenant; the guide is in the archive.
job.guide: Open the guide in the archive

powershell.title: Commands for Exchange Online PowerShell
powershell.intro: Instead of the steps above, an administrator of the Microsoft 365 tenant can run these commands. They create the connector to this installation, set the mailbox for undeliverable journal reports and create the journal rule for all mail.
powershell.ndrHint: A real mailbox of the tenant that someone reads, such as a shared mailbox. Exchange sends reports there that could not reach {appName}.

ndrProblem.empty: Enter the mailbox for undeliverable journal reports.
ndrProblem.journal_address: This is the journal address itself. Enter a mailbox of the tenant.
ndrProblem.journal_host: This address is at the journal host. Enter a mailbox of the tenant.

powershell.needsNdr: The commands appear once the mailbox for undeliverable journal reports is entered.

firstReport.hint: Send a mail within the organisation after setting up the rule. The page then checks every 5 seconds whether its report arrived.
firstReport.waitingHint: Checking every 5 seconds. A report usually arrives within a few minutes of the mail.
firstReport.expired: No report arrived within 30 minutes. Check the connector, the journal rule and the firewall, and the mailbox for undeliverable journal reports.

flags.report-unparseable: Journal report could not be parsed
flags.report-parse-timeout: Journal report could not be read in time; archived byte for byte as received, without its details
flags.report-parse-memory-limit: Journal report needed more memory to read than allowed; archived byte for byte as received, without its details
flags.envelope-unparseable: Envelope text could not be parsed
flags.original-message-missing: Original message missing; the raw report was archived instead
flags.original-message-unparseable: Original message could not be parsed
flags.recipient-classification-degraded: To/Cc/Bcc could not be determined for every recipient
flags.recipients-truncated: More than 100,000 recipients; only the first 100,000 are listed (the archived report keeps all of them)
flags.captured-late: Captured afterwards: in the mailbox before capture started
flags.message-id-conflict: Another archived mail has the same Message-ID but different content

filesystem.title: Protected by {appName} only
filesystem.description: The archive is on a filesystem (local storage or NFS). {appName} neither changes nor deletes archived mail before its retention ends, and the hash chain makes changes detectable. Anyone with access to the server or the storage can still change or delete the files.

s3_locked.title: Object Lock on, with a limitation
s3_locked.description: The bucket enforces Object Lock. In this version {appName} locks the archive item records with it, but not yet the packs that hold the message content. The content is, as on a filesystem, protected by {appName} and the hash chain only.

s3_unlocked.title: No Object Lock
s3_unlocked.description: The bucket does not enforce Object Lock. Archived mail is protected by {appName} and the hash chain only: anyone with write access to the bucket can change or delete objects.

s3_unknown.title: Object Lock not checked
s3_unknown.description: Whether the bucket enforces Object Lock is not known. Test the repository. Until then, archived mail is protected by {appName} and the hash chain only.

unknown.title: Protection unknown
unknown.description: The archive's repository could not be determined.

capture.title: Capture from the mailboxes
capture.description: How mail reaches the archive from the mailboxes themselves: Microsoft Graph for Microsoft 365, IMAP archiving for IMAP accounts. Both capture near-time, shortly after delivery; journaling and forwarding below capture at transport.

unused.graph_sync: No mail job captures Microsoft 365 mailboxes by Graph.
unused.imap_sync: No mail job captures IMAP accounts by IMAP archiving.

mailboxes.title: Per mailbox
mailboxes.resyncDone: {mailbox} is caught up on the next pass.

hold.title: Deleted mail in Microsoft 365
hold.description: Graph captures mail shortly after delivery. So that mail deleted right away is still captured, a retention policy or a litigation hold should keep deleted mail in the tenant. {appName} cannot read that from Graph: check it with the commands and confirm it here.
hold.why: {count, plural, one {# mailbox is} other {# mailboxes are}} captured by Graph. Without a hold, mail deleted right after delivery can be missing.
hold.commands: Exchange Online PowerShell: show retention policies and holds
hold.confirmDescription: You confirm that a retention policy or litigation hold keeps deleted mail of the archived mailboxes in this tenant. The confirmation is recorded with your name in the audit log.
hold.withdrawDescription: The archive page then shows again that no hold is confirmed. The withdrawal is recorded in the audit log.

forwarding.title: Forwarding to the archive
forwarding.description: For IMAP accounts whose job chose forwarding: the mail provider sends a copy of every incoming and outgoing mail to an address of {appName}. The copy is made at transport, before the user can change or delete the mail. Each account has its own address, so every copy belongs to the right mailbox.
forwarding.empty: No mail job has chosen forwarding for its IMAP accounts. Choose it in the job's capture ways.
forwarding.googleUsesTenant: Routing rule to the tenant's journal address (tab Google Workspace)

rotate.title: Renew the archive address of {account}?
rotate.description: A new address replaces the current one. The current address stops working at once: copies sent to it are refused.
rotate.consequence: Change the address in the provider's rule right away, otherwise copies are missing until then.
rotate.done: New archive address created. Change it at the provider now.

setup.title: Set up at the provider
setup.needsAddress: Create the archive addresses of the accounts first; the configuration then appears here.
setup.someMissing: Accounts without an address are not included yet.

postfix.intro: Postfix copies every mail by sender and by recipient to the address in a map: incoming mail of the account by recipient, outgoing mail by sender.
postfix.reload: Build the map and reload Postfix

mailcow.intro: In mailcow under E-Mail, Configuration, BCC, add a sender map and a recipient map for each account, each with its archive address as BCC destination.

sieve.intro: Where the provider runs Sieve, a rule per account redirects a copy of every incoming mail; the mail itself stays in the mailbox.
sieve.outgoing: Sieve runs on delivery only: for outgoing mail the provider also needs a BCC rule by sender.

google.intro: Google Workspace routes a copy of every mail to the tenant's journal address. {appName} assigns each copy to the accounts it names in its headers.

steps.open: Open the Google Admin console: Apps, Google Workspace, Gmail, Routing.
steps.rule: Under Routing, add a rule and give it a name.
steps.messages: Messages to affect: Inbound, Outbound, “Internal: sending” and “Internal: receiving”.
steps.recipient: For the messages above: Also deliver to, Add more recipients, the address below.
steps.save: Save the rule. Changes can take up to an hour.

google.noAddress: The journal address cannot be shown: no valid journal host is configured.
